operating_mode.input: You take in raw material through the Direct Resource channel: a framework, a past case, a credential, a standard you already hold. The month and hour branches both hide Direct Resource, and it weighs six — a substantial store you draw on. But the loop shows the intake is often defensive: you collect one more source, one more precedent, before you let the output out. The new input that actually widens your range — an unfamiliar problem, a different field, a course outside your toolkit — arrives less often, because the Seven Killings filter in the year stem trains you to check before you speak. So what you take in is real and solid, but it tends to reinforce what you already know rather than stretch it.
operating_mode.processing: Your processing is fast and outward-facing. Eating God is the leading force and jointly heaviest with Companion, and the day branch itself is Eating God. You do not sit with a problem for long before you are sketching a fix, drafting the email, or saying the blunt version out loud. The processing is not deliberation — it is production. You think by making. When the first draft meets resistance, you switch to the Direct Resource store: you pull up the old document, cite the standard, and anchor the next version. That switch is smooth because the base is already sufficient — the Day Master is slightly strong, so Resource is a store you draw on, not a shortage you must fill.
operating_mode.output: You output a working version, not a polished one. The Eating God at the leading weight means the draft, the fix, the straight opinion is how you engage. You feel more alive after a session where you produced something concrete than after a day of listening and planning. The Companion weight at eight means the output often happens next to someone — you pair, split the work, check in at short intervals. The output is co-produced as much as it is solo. What you ship is usually a rough prototype that lets others react, and that is the point: the output is designed to generate feedback, not to be final.
operating_mode.recovery: You recharge by producing again, not by resting. The loop turns: output runs into a wall, you fall back on the Direct Resource base, and that base lets you produce again. Recovery is the moment the base gets refreshed — when new input actually gets used, when the Bing Zi luck pillar starting around age forty-two brings water into the branch and makes new material easier to absorb. But the loop only recharges if the base is growing. If you keep drawing on the same store without topping it up, the recovery is fake — you are recycling, not recharging. The real recovery is a fixed block each week to study something outside your current toolkit, then finishing one small piece of output from it before the week ends.

failure_environments.env: An environment that punishes the blunt version and rewards waiting — where every draft must be pre-approved, where a rough prototype is treated as a mistake, and where you are the only one pushing while others only discuss.
failure_environments.mechanism: This environment trains the Seven Killings filter in the year stem harder. The filter is the earliest position, the first check before you speak, and when the culture rewards caution, that check becomes a gate. The Eating God output at the leading weight goes underground — you still produce, but you produce silently, in folders, in evening drafts you never ship. The Direct Resource base stops growing because new input never gets used, and the loop starts recycling the same store. The failure is not that you stop working; it is that the work stops widening. You keep producing from the same template, and the range of what you can produce narrows.

failure_environments.env: An environment where you are the only one pushing — no co-producer, no peer who will actually do something rather than only discuss it.
failure_environments.mechanism: Companion is jointly heaviest with Eating God, and the hour stem is Companion. You do your best work next to someone who is also building. When you are the only one pushing, the Companion energy has no outlet, and the loop loses its co-production segment. You lose momentum, not because you lack talent, but because the mode of working alongside others is a natural mode, not a preference. The output gets delayed, the feedback cycle stretches, and the Eating God energy turns into frustration rather than production. The failure mechanism is a missing peer, not a missing skill.

failure_environments.env: An environment that rewards early drafts and fast feedback but never brings new input — a team that reacts quickly to what you produce but never exposes you to an unfamiliar problem, a different field, or a course outside your toolkit.
failure_environments.mechanism: This environment looks good because the output flows, but it starves the Direct Resource base. The loop turns smoothly on recycled material. You produce more, but the range of what you produce stops widening. The Direct Resource at six is a store, and a store that is never topped up eventually runs thin. The failure is slow: the first few months feel productive, then the last three outputs share the same structure, and you notice the new input you collected has not changed what you produce. The environment enables output but suppresses growth.

ideal_life_structure.time: You need a time structure that protects a fixed block each week for new input — study, a course, an unfamiliar problem — and a separate block for shipping one small piece of output from it before the week ends. The Eating God output at the leading weight means you produce best in short cycles, not long projects. A week is a natural unit: input early, output by the end. The Direct Resource base at six means the study block is not optional — it is the segment that keeps the loop from recycling. Without it, the time structure collapses into production from the same store, and the work starts to repeat itself.
ideal_life_structure.collaboration: You need a collaboration density of at least one co-producer — someone who is also building, who will split the work and check in at short intervals. The Companion weight at eight means this is a natural mode, not a preference. The collaboration should be action-oriented: you call the colleague who will actually do something, not the one who will only discuss it. A team of two or three builders is better than a large committee. The collaboration density should be high enough that you are never the only one pushing, but low enough that the output does not get filtered through layers of approval.
ideal_life_structure.feedback_cycle: You need a feedback cycle measured in days, not months. The Eating God output is a rough prototype designed to generate reaction, and the loop turns cleanly when the reaction comes back fast. If your team reacts to a rough draft within a day, the output gets used immediately, the Companion energy finds a co-producer, and the Direct Resource base gets refreshed instead of recycled. A long feedback cycle — a quarterly review, a pre-approval process — trains the Seven Killings filter and pushes the output underground. The ideal cycle is short enough that you can ship, react, and ship again within the same week.
ideal_life_structure.income_rhythm: Your income rhythm suits project-based or output-based compensation more than a fixed salary tied to tenure. The Eating God at the leading weight means you are paid for what you produce, and the Companion weight means co-production is part of the value. A rhythm that rewards shipped work — a project fee, a product launch, a consulting engagement — fits the loop better than a rhythm that rewards waiting and seniority. The Direct Resource base at six means you can also draw on credentials and standards, so a hybrid rhythm — a base retainer plus output-based upside — matches the structure: the retainer is the store, the upside is the output.

stability_vs_volatility.verdict: You are better suited to a moderate-variance life structure — stable enough to protect the Direct Resource base, variable enough to keep the Eating God output flowing. Pure stability suppresses the output; pure volatility starves the base.
stability_vs_volatility.reason: The Day Master is slightly strong, and Eating God at nine and Companion at eight dominate. Output is a favorable direction, which means the structure wants to produce and ship. But the Direct Resource at six is the segment that lets the output continue — it is the store you draw on when the output runs into a wall. A high-variance life with no base starves that store, and the loop recycles. A pure-stability life with no output pressure trains the Seven Killings filter and pushes the Eating God underground. The moderate-variance structure — a stable base plus output-based upside — is the form the innate talents can actually deliver.
stability_vs_volatility.precondition: The precondition is that the base keeps growing. The Direct Resource store must be topped up with new input on a regular cadence — a course, a different project, an unfamiliar problem — or the moderate-variance structure collapses into recycling. The Bing Zi luck pillar starting around age forty-two brings water into the branch, which makes new input easier to absorb, but the defensive habit is what resists it. The precondition is not 'try harder'; it is 'use the new input before the week ends.' Without that, the variance produces output from the same store, and the range stops widening.

environment_checklist: Does this environment react to a rough draft within a day, or does every output need pre-approval? If the feedback cycle is measured in weeks or months, the Seven Killings filter gets trained harder and the Eating God output goes underground.

Is there at least one co-producer — someone who is also building and will actually do something, not only discuss it? If you are the only one pushing, the Companion energy has no outlet and you lose momentum, not because you lack talent but because co-production is a natural mode.

Does the environment bring new input on a regular cadence — an unfamiliar problem, a different field, a course outside your toolkit? If the output flows but the input never arrives, the Direct Resource base starves and the loop recycles the same store.

Does the compensation reward shipped work — a project fee, a product launch, an output-based upside — or does it reward waiting and seniority? The Eating God at the leading weight means you are paid for what you produce, and a rhythm that rewards waiting suppresses the output.

Can you protect a fixed block each week for study and ship one small piece of output from it before the week ends? If the time structure leaves no room for new input, the base stops growing and the moderate-variance structure collapses into recycling.
